messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GeoDNS health check spike — Cloudflare resolvers (eu-west-1 egress) reporting elevated NXDOMAINs for service.rwd.io (rate: 6.2% over baseline). Paging on-call.
leo_oncall: I see it, getting paged. Beginning triage — marking impact: partial (some AZs). @sara_sre you on call for network today?
sara_sre: on it. quick blurb: customers in eu-west are seeing intermittent 502s and some DNS failures. Canary probes show inconsistent answers between AZ-a and AZ-c.
devin_net: reproducing with dig from inside EU egress:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 service.rwd.io +short
<empty> ;; NXDOMAIN
$ dig @8.8.8.8 service.rwd.io +short
10.10.20.30
```
so some external resolvers returning NXDOMAINs, others OK. looks like cached negative responses on Cloudflare's edge that are sticky to clients routed through AZ-c egress.
maria_platform: checking geodns control plane — no config change for that zone in last 48h. Route53 records show healthy NS set. TTL currently 300s.
leo_oncall: quick mitigation idea: reduce TTL to 60, flush Cloudflare cache for the zone, and fail traffic from the az-c egress to az-a via smart routing. can we do that quickly?
sara_sre: we can push route-level reroute: update routing policy to prefer eu-west-1a for new queries. preparing change — will run safe rollout (canary 5% -> 100%)
devin_net: cloudflare cache purge submitted (via API) — job id cf-purge-9921. also filed ticket with CF support referencing sticky NX for negative answers.
leo_oncall: customer success ping — Julie, any noisy customer reports?
customer_success_julie: yes, two customers (acme-inc, fintech-x) reported errors starting ~T-18m. Both had partial fail rates ~8-12% on user endpoints. They're on eu-west regions. I've opened support cases and asked for status page update once we confirm mitigation.
sara_sre: change to routing policy initiated:
```
# geodns rollout
set policy prefer eu-west-1a for zone service.rwd.io canary=0.05
```
rolling to 100% now. monitoring delta.
incident_bot: Deploybot: route change applied to geodns (commit rwd/geodns@c7d3). Canary success 5/5 checks. Promoting.
leo_oncall: trace from affected host after reroute shows answers restored:
```
$ dig @1.1.1.1 service.rwd.io +short
10.10.20.30
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" https://service.rwd.io/health
200 0.142s
```
devin_net: Observability: Cloudflare negative cache rate trending down after purge + routing change. NX rate back to baseline ~0.2%.
maria_platform: TTL change to 60 applied to zone to reduce cache lifetime. note: will increase queries for ~10m while caches refill.
customer_success_julie: notified customers, will update once SLO verified. they appreciated the quick re-route.
sara_sre: root cause hypothesis: transient egress path sticky to a subset of Cloudflare resolvers that had stale negative cache for our name due to earlier probe that got NX (possibly due to a short-lived auth failure at our authoritative layer). Because some AZs route through that egress pool, clients in those AZs saw NX while others didn't.
leo_oncall: next steps: 1) follow up with CF ticket for root cause on their side (ticket cf-8791), 2) run retro within 48h to confirm authoritative timing and monitor TTLs, 3) evaluate lowering negative caching TTL at authoritative side if possible.
devin_net: adding synthetic probes routed through all egress pools to detect early NX skew. will ship rule rwd/probes@t1.
maria_platform: logging note: cloudwatch alarms triggered for DNS-NX spike; will keep for 12h with elevated sensitivity.
incident_bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED: service.rwd.io DNS NX spike mitigated. Postmortem ping scheduled for 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC. /cc @sara_sre @devin_net @leo_oncall
leo_oncall: thanks team. I'll keep the channel open for any followups and close after postmortem link posted. :thumbsup:
